guard: a newer cotal announces a shared seed-store migration, persists its writer and timestamp, and an older cotal reports that provenance when it refuses the store
why: THREE MUTATIONS, one for each externally visible part of the contract.
M1 deletes the migration announcement after the new stamp commits. The store still advances and
the provenance still persists, so only the operator-visible migration cell turns red.
M2 writes the legacy generation-only stamp. The migration still announces, but the durable record
cannot tell a later older CLI which executable wrote it or when. The writer cell is the first red.
M3 suppresses the provenance suffix on the downgrade refusal. The stored fields remain intact,
which distinguishes a reporting regression from a persistence regression.
All anchors are unique code-only spans. Each mutation is compile-clean and restores a concrete
failure mode rather than restating an assertion inside the product.

mutations.name: the generation advances silently because the migration announcement is deleted
mutations.expectRed: ✗ FAIL: migration provenance: a newer binary announces the shared seed-store generation migration
mutations.cell: ✗ FAIL: migration provenance: a newer binary announces the shared seed-store generation migration

mutations.name: the committed stamp drops writer and timestamp provenance
mutations.expectRed: ✗ FAIL: migration provenance: stamp records the exact CLI entry that wrote the generation
mutations.cell: ✗ FAIL: migration provenance: stamp records the exact CLI entry that wrote the generation

mutations.name: the downgrade refusal hides the stored writer and timestamp
mutations.expectRed: ✗ FAIL: downgrade: the refusal names who wrote the newer generation and when
mutations.cell: ✗ FAIL: downgrade: the refusal names who wrote the newer generation and when
